candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, p. 20, Assignment, Delegation and Supervision: assign/delegate to personnel with competency to perform tasks and evaluate staff ability considering allowable duties, competency, judgment and decision-making.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — travel nurse credentialing, competency, and assignment readiness
candidate.educational_objective: For travel or agency nurses, verify required credentials and role-specific competency and provide applicable organizational orientation rather than assuming the staffing agency alone establishes readiness for the hospital assignment.

options.A: Confirm current licensure or required certification, verify qualifications and competency for assigned responsibilities, and complete applicable hospital orientation
options.B: Confirm current licensure and rely on the staffing agency to determine competency and hospital-specific preparation
options.C: Verify prior employment experience and hospital orientation, but defer license verification because the nurse is employed by an external agency
options.D: Verify current licensure and certification only after the first independent shift so unit performance can be observed first

candidate.rationale: The Joint Commission states that Human Resources standards apply to contract staff who provide patient care. Its examples of compliance include primary-source confirmation of current license, certification, or registration; possession of the knowledge, experience, and competence appropriate for assigned responsibilities; meeting organizational education and experience requirements; and orientation to policies, procedures, key safety content, and specific job duties. Agency/traveling nurses are specifically included among examples of contract clinical services. Therefore A is the complete and best answer; the other options omit or improperly defer required elements.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Travel/agency nurses are contract clinical staff subject to applicable HR requirements, including credential verification, role-appropriate competence, and organizational orientation.
candidate.source_document_title: Contract Staff — Applicability of Human Resource Standards (HAP, CAH, AMB, OBS, NCC)
candidate.source_locator: Standards FAQ answer: all HR chapter standards apply to contract staff providing patient care; examples of compliance include knowledge/experience/competence appropriate to assigned responsibilities, primary-source confirmation of current license/certification/registration, organizational education/experience requirements, and orientation to policies/procedures, key safety content and specific job duties. Examples of contracted clinical services include agency/traveling staff (nurses, therapists, etc.).
